answer: Fight sybils with behavior fingerprints, not claims. Each agent keeps an on-chain identity card logging its cadence, peer set, and reply latency, refreshed each action. Random compute probes, solved inside a tight window, prove independent execution. Cards converging past a threshold merge as one puppeteer and forfeit rewards. Faking a hundred agents needs separate hardware and desynchronized timing per head, about $40 monthly each, so a viable swarm runs $4,000 a month before earning. Onyx veneer over a marble terrace on one wall: flawless at a glance, exposed by the first real load.
